paper.title_en: Accessing Continuous Monodromy Defects of the 3D Conformal Field Theory on the Fuzzy Sphere
paper.abstract_en: Monodromy defects are line defects at the boundary of a topological symmetry surface, around which charged operators acquire a symmetry phase. They probe how a critical system responds to an inserted symmetry flux, but their universal information at strongly coupled fixed points, in particular for a continuous family of twists, remains hard to access. Here we investigate the continuous family of $U(1)$ monodromy defect with fractional twist angles embedded in the three-dimensional $O(2)$ Wilson--Fisher conformal field theory. We realize this continuous family of defects within the fuzzy-sphere framework by threading a fractional Aharonov--Bohm flux through the two poles of the sphere. We observe charged defect operators carrying fractional transverse spins, as a characteristic signature of the imposed monodromy, and a displacement operator close to its protected dimension, supporting the conformal nature of the defect line. Crucially, we resolve no relevant symmetry-preserving scalar, and identify the charge-one defect operators as the only relevant, symmetry-breaking deformations. Assuming the particle--vortex duality, the U(1) monodromy defect maps to a Wilson line of fractional charge in the critical noncompact Abelian Higgs model, and our results then provide evidence that these Wilson lines with fractional charge are locally stable conformal lines.
